name: Fundal height
seoTitle: Fundal height Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Fundal height: work out expected SFH from the GA days and the fetal weight. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Fundal height calculator turns the GA days and the fetal weight into expected SFH. Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Fundal height calculator work?
sections.html:
The Fundal height calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports expected SFH in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the calculation type, the mother's weight and the vertex); then you type in the GA days and the fetal weight.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as SFH percentile, SFH to gestational age and SFH to fetal weight. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A number, expressed in #.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as >91 kg (200lb) and ≤91 kg (200lb). The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as above ischial spine and below isichial spine. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in grams. The unit chip switches it to any of the 29 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in weeks / days. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.

3 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Fundal height calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Expected SFH=-289 ÷ 12500 × (GA ^ 2) × the natural log of (GA) + (529 ÷ 5000) × (GA ^ 2) + 51333 ÷ 10000
SFH standard deviation (SD)=((129 ÷ 5000) × GA + 9923 ÷ 10000)
GA weeks=GA − 1 ÷ 7 × GA days
Gestational age=-27073 ÷ 10000 × the square root of (measured SFH) + (1619 ÷ 1250) × measured SFH + 32929 ÷ 5000
Measured SFH=(1 ÷ 155) × fetal weight + vertex + mother's weight

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Open the page and it is already filled in. With the values it starts from — Calculation type set to SFH percentile, GA weeks = 16, GA days = 0 and Mother's weight set to ≤91 kg (200lb) — it reports Expected SFH = 1580.7924 cm and SFH standard deviation (SD) = 140.51 cm.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Expected SFH = 1580.7924 cm and SFH standard deviation (SD) = 140.51 cm should be roughly the size you expected from Calculation type set to SFH percentile and GA weeks = 16.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Time, opening in weeks / days
  • Mass, opening in grams
  • Time, opening in weeks / days

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Fundal height calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the GA days and the fetal weight — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Fundal height calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns expected SFH, derived from the GA days and the fetal weight. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Fundal height calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the GA days and the fetal weight, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter measured SFH in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Measured SFH opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Expected SFH = 1580.7924 cm. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Fundal height calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
